flavor_spans.text: It's quiet. Your footsteps are soft on the carpet. How can a staircase be so long?

Hot summer winds blew
the day you walked in.
But in here,
stale air.

Cold feet on the landing.
Each wing is harder than the last.
The inner room is climbed
step by step.

The tiles weren't enough.
The yen wasn't enough either.
One more wing,
that will be enough.
In the storeroom, tea sets sit in lacquer boxes with the cups already poured. No one has touched them. The House has little patience for ceremony.

One lantern
shows the next step.
The rest of the wing
is
dark.
Someone scratched a tally into the bannister — seven marks, then eight, then the numbers stop and start again lower down, as if the wall moved overnight.

The door you came through
is not the door
you leave by.
You stopped checking
after the third wing.

Dust falls
through a shaft
with no window above it.
The inner room
must be
near.
A cracked screen in the corridor shows another table, another hand being played, always one move ahead of yours. You walk faster. The image does not change.

After the ordeal
this staircase feels longer.
It wasn't longer yesterday.
You know it wasn't.
When you fell last time, The House took your yen and your relics. You started again with someone else's leftovers in your pockets and pretended that was a fresh beginning.

A tile
face-down
on the carpet.
Not yours.
Not yet.
The House rewards a fat purse with interest, the way a host refills your cup so you'll stay at the table. You know who wins in aggregate. You stay anyway.

The storeroom remembers
its losers
displayed and priced.
You browse
your predecessors.
"We have a winner! You, our most honored contestant and guest!" A banner said that. The banner has been here longer than you have.

They say the sealed table
is one wing deeper.
You've heard that
since wing one.
Tiles clack somewhere behind the wall — a full hand being played in a room with no door. You pause on the landing. The sound stops when you listen for it.
The gambling house shut its doors to the world years ago. Inside, the lamps still burn. You wonder who keeps the ledger.

Your footsteps
and another
one echo behind.
You stop.
Silence.

The outer wings are cluttered — racks, screens, closed doors.
Deeper in, it gets quieter.
The quiet feels like
certainty.

Thirty-seven steps
this landing.
Yesterday
there were forty-one.
A hope-shattered gambler sat on this step once. The cushion still holds his shape. You sit beside it and don't ask how long they've been gone.
